question.problem: A bag contains $4$ five-dollar bills, $8$ ten-dollar bills, and $6$ twenty-dollar bills. If one bill is randomly drawn from a bag, what is its expected value?
question.worked_solution:
The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Let $X$ be the value of a randomly drawn bill. Then the support is $S=\{5,10,20\}.$

In the bag there are  $4$ five-dollar bills, $8$ ten-dollar bills and $6$ twenty-dollar bills (eighteen bills in total), so the probabilities are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5) & =\frac{4}{18}=\frac{2}{9} \\ P(10) & =\frac{8}{18}=\frac{4}{9} \\ P(20) & =\frac{6}{18}=\frac{3}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =5\cdot f(5)+10\cdot f(10)+20\cdot f(20) \\  & =5(\frac{2}{9})+10(\frac{4}{9})+20(\frac{3}{9}) \\  & =\frac{10}{9}+\frac{40}{9}+\frac{60}{9} \\  & =\frac{10+40+60}{9} \\  & =\frac{110}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
